A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMMAX framework and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 7 and Tables 1–3 report original multiclass experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny ImageNet, plus binary classification experiments using linear models.

after.justification: Section 7 and Tables 1–3 retain the authors' original multiclass and binary classification results. Results retained from v1 still qualify.

M1.justification: The binary and multiclass IMMAX objectives, class-dependent margin scaling, regularization and prediction rules are retained. The revised hyperparameter search specification changes experimental tuning, without introducing a new algorithm component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three datasets under long-tailed and step imbalance at ratios 200, 100 and 10, and the same airplane, automobile and horse one-versus-rest CIFAR-10 tasks. The new discussion of balanced data, large-scale datasets and contrastive learning adds no evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain CE, RW, BS, EQUAL, LA, CB, FOCAL and LDAM; Table 3 retains HINGE and LDAM. Figure 1 retains the SVM and Cao et al. comparisons. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B replaces IMMAX's search interval centered at rho*_k with radius 5 and step size 1 by a relative interval with radius approximately 0.8 rho*_k and approximately ten candidates. This revises a previously stated tuning protocol; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. Other stated training and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a brief qualitative assessment that performance is insensitive to margin variations within the search neighborhood. Section 8 also reports minimal performance impact from sharing rare-class margins. These additions lack quantitative sweeps or detailed ablation protocols; Figure 1 and existing baseline-tuning observations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state five runs and report means with standard deviations. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced. The approximately ten tuning candidates in v2 are not repeated runs.

E6.justification: All 171 mean/standard-deviation pairs in Tables 1–3 are identical, and Figure 1 retains its findings. V2 newly reports qualitative insensitivity to local margin variations and minimal performance impact from margin sharing, without numerical outcomes for these assertions.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds an assertion that the H-consistency bounds extend to uniformly bounded hypothesis sets with complexity dependence, without supplying the extended bound or proof. Existing theorem statements and Appendix C–F proofs are retained. The multiclass lemma and theorem newly displayed in Section 5 already appeared in v1's Appendix E.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its novelty framing: v1 identifies Cao et al. as the only prior generalization analysis, while v2 acknowledges additional analyses and emphasizes their balanced-loss target. The abstract, contribution summary and conclusion retain the same principal IMMAX, consistency and generalization claims.

C2.justification: The new Section 8 discusses reduction to standard methods on balanced data, scalability relative to cross-entropy training, and interpretation as class-dependent temperature scaling with connections to contrastive learning. These extend the applicability and mechanism discussion; the existing accuracy-versus-balanced-accuracy qualification and interpretation of benchmark results remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B replaces the fixed-width IMMAX tuning instructions with scale-dependent intervals and an approximate candidate count. Sharing margins across minority classes was already documented in v1. Baseline loss definitions, other hyperparameter ranges and training details are retained, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: Section 1 and Appendix A newly credit generalization analyses by already-cited Jiawei et al. (2020) and newly cited Wang et al. (2023). V2 also adds the Khosla et al. contrastive-learning connection and further consistency and optimization references. These refine the existing positioning without replacing its broader related-work account.

P1.justification: V2 adds a Discussion section before the conclusion, acknowledgements and an impact statement, and brings existing multiclass statements into the main text. Local explanations, cross-references, author information and bibliography formatting are edited, while most prose and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, with denser appendix formatting and revised headers. Figure 1 and Tables 1–3 are resized and repositioned; Tables 1 and 2 now appear side by side. This substantially changes visual presentation while retaining their scientific content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves research positioning by acknowledging additional prior generalization analyses. Appendix B replaces a search interval extending below the required positive margins with a positive, scale-dependent specification, improving reproducibility. The discussion and main-text presentation of existing multiclass guarantees improve accessibility. Gains remain limited: numerical evidence and proofs are unchanged, and the new sensitivity and bounded-hypothesis extension assertions lack quantitative support or an additional proof.
